2026 Audi Q3 And Toyota RAV4 PHEV Underperform In IIHS Updated Moderate Overlap Crash Test

CA
By Chloe Adams Car Culture & Restomod Editor • via Jalopnik Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Jalopnik Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • You may think that all modern cars offer unimpeachable protection for their occupants in the event of a crash, but there's more variance and nuance in modern crash safety than you might be aware of.
  • The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety or IIHS , published its first crash test ratings 30-years ago , in the year I was born, 1995.
  • Official reporting verified via Jalopnik news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • CHLOE ADAMS Car Culture & Restomod Editor

Heritage Preservation vs Modern Performance

Automotive passion is increasingly defined by the synthesis of analog soul and contemporary engineering. This coverage from Jalopnik illustrates how bespoke builders, private collectors, and restomod artists are preserving the golden eras of internal combustion while adopting carbon fiber composites and precision craftsmanship.

Big Picture: Auction hammer prices and enthusiast demand indicate sustained historical appreciation for rare, analog driver's vehicles.

You may think that all modern cars offer unimpeachable protection for their occupants in the event of a crash, but there's more variance and nuance in modern crash safety than you might be aware of. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety or IIHS , published its first crash test ratings 30-years ago , in the year I was born, 1995. In those early days, its tests were criticized by automakers for being too severe, and yet those same automakers ended up building safer cars that aced the same tests just a few years later.

📌 The Core Development

As the American automotive landscape continues to evolve, the IIHS has evolved its tests , too, with the introduction of updated tests, like the new whiplash prevention test , the updated moderate front overlap test, and the updated side impact crash test that the 2026 Cadillac CT5 recently failed spectacularly . The tests conducted by the IIHS are extremely specific and controlled scenarios, but they establish an objective baseline by which to measure many areas of crash protection. The updates in IIHS tests over the years have uncovered new areas of vulnerability in some cars , and the latest crop of cars tested produced some unexpected results and clear weak points, specifically from cars like the all-new Audi Q3 and Toyota RAV4 .

Let's start with the ever-popular Toyota RAV4. The IIHS just released results from the updated moderate overlap crash test for the redesigned 2026 Toyota RAV4 and RAV4 Plug-In Hybrid , and neither one earned the highest rating of Good. The RAV4 Hybrid earned the second-highest score of Acceptable, and the RAV4 PHEV earned the second-lowest score of Marginal in this test. Though these two cars are very similar, their different powertrains affect their performance in a variety of ways, including the PHEV's increased curb weight.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

These less-than-perfect ratings are based on the way that the RAV4 protects the rear-seat passenger. In the regular RAV4 Hybrid, which earned the second-highest score of Acceptable, the rear passenger dummy recorded injury values that indicate a moderate risk of injury to the head or neck and chest, because the shoulder belt moved too far up toward the dummy's neck, compromising its effectiveness. It earned Acceptable ratings for rear passenger head and neck injuries, chest injuries, and the performance of its rear restraints.

The Marginal-rated RAV4 PHEV faced similar challenges with the performance of the rear-seat restraint system since its shoulder belt also moved toward the dummy's neck, but the lap belt also moved from its ideal position on the pelvis, up onto the abdomen, which increases the risk of abdominal injuries. The latter issue is a common reason why many new cars don't perform well in the updated moderate overlap crash test. When the lap belt remains in its ideal position on the big bony pelvis, it safely restrains the occupant without risking organ damage, but when the lap belt slips and cuts into the unprotected, organ-filled abdomen, it naturally poses additional injury risk.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

The also-new Audi Q3 scored the IIHS lowest rating of Poor in the updated moderate overlap crash test for similar reasons to the RAV4. The Q3's biggest points of concern were a moderate risk of rear-seat occupant chest injury due to the shoulder belt slipping up toward the dummy's neck, and a Poor rating for the rear passenger restraints and dummy kinematics. The rear lap belt also moved from its ideal position securing the dummy's pelvis to the soft and vulnerable abdomen. It received Good ratings for its protection of the dummy's thighs as well as its head and neck, though.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

The latest crop of updated moderate overlap test results also includes the 2026 and 2027 Nissan Kicks, 2026 Chevrolet Trailblazer, and the 2027 Volkswagen Jetta. Both the Nissan Kicks and the 2027 Volkswagen Jetta earned the top score of Good in the updated moderate overlap front crash test, but the 2026 Trailblazer earned the lowest rating of Poor.

The IIHS subjects cars to a barrage of different evaluations, including the small overlap front crash test, the updated side impact test, and front crash prevention tests with both vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-pedestrian scenarios. The institute evaluates their headlights, seat belt reminders, and the ease-of-use of their LATCH child seat anchors. There's a lot to cover there, and standards are always getting tougher.
